newsitem.title: INDIA: Russian defence minister to sign deals with India.
newsitem.headline: Russian defence minister to sign deals with India.

text.p: Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov arrived in New Delhi on Monday on a three-day visit to sign a defence cooperation agreement including the supply of warplanes to India, officials of both countries said.
The visit is the first by a Russian defence minister to India, which was a close ally of the former Soviet Union.
Rodionov was expected to sign defence deals on the supply of 40 Sukhoi SU-30MK long-range fighter bombers and MSTA-S self-propelled howitzers, the Press Trust of India said.

Rodionov will meet Indian leaders, including Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav and External Affairs Minister I.K. Gujral. He is also scheduled to meet the chiefs of India's defence forces, an Indian defence ministry official said.
PTI said agreements on the training of Indian military personnel and a new service-to-service exchange between the armed forces of the two countries were likely to be finalised.
As the former Soviet Union's main non-communist ally, India was one of Moscow's biggest arms clients.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin, visiting New Delhi in 1993, signed a treaty resolving a thorny debt issue that had curtailed supplies of defence equipment.
Yeltsin pledged to transfer technology, establish joint ventures and set up factories in India to ensure an adequate supply of spare parts for India's military.
